To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the number of c-FOS immunoreactive cells in the preoptical and paraventricolar nuclei of the hypothalamus increases in lactating mothers compared to virgins and non-lactating mothers, and that the number of these cells in the ventromedials hypothalamic nucleus is higher in virgin rabbits compared to lactating mothers.
the c-FOS expression was stimulated in several forebrain structures of mother rabbits after nursing.
nursing increases the expression of the immediate early gene c-FOS in the forebrain structures of the rabbit mother.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of brain structures involved in the regulation of the circadian rhythm of maternal care and of the milk ejection reflex.
identifying neural structures involved in the control of maternal behavior.
identifying brain regions that participate in the control of maternal behavior and milk letdown in the rabbit.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the POA is involved in the establishment of motherliness, the LS in the maintenance of the motherly behavior, and the magnocellular nuclei in milk letdown.
the motherhood and nursing stimulate FOS expression in the brain of rabbits.
the c-Fos expression is a reliable marker for identifying the brain structures that regulate maternal behavior in mammals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the POA is the key structure for maternal behavior in this species, and the LS and magnocellular nuclei are important structures for the expression of specific aspects of the behavior.
nursing stimulates c-FOS expression and the expression is more intense on PPD 3 than on PPD 2.
the preoptic area and the lateral septum are involved in establishing the motherhood state and that the paraventricular nucleus and the supraoptic nucleus are involved in the milk letdown reflex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain is a key player in maternal behavior.
c-FOS is an important tool in the investigation of the neural basis of maternal behavior.
nursing stimulates c-FOS expression, which may be involved in regulating the mother’s behavior.
